summary: Backend-only independent verification of Lex 2.0 Phase 2E corrections. No paid LLM and no Tavily calls (AIA_NO_PAID=1; LLM and deadline extraction mocked; legislation _fetch mocked, plus 2 free live legislation.gov.uk lookups). I re-ran every suite the main agent listed, one file per pytest run. All passed: phase2e 35, stage2_safety 44, phase2d 21, phase1 16, acas_deadlines 13, date_guard 12, 2a1_review 5, 2a1_confidence_facts 8, phase1_wiring 4, customer_test1 12, free_official_fallback 5, 2c_law_watch 43, 2b_reasoning 34, 2a3 45, 2a2 91, financial_safeguards 18, pass_queue 12. Offline eval passed 117/117. I also wrote a new probe file of 34 tests for edge cases: 23 pass and 11 fail. The failures come from 1 medium defect that drops the guidance block in chat, plus several minor regex false positives. Confirmed working: guidance is wired for Free (haiku), Plus (gpt-5.2, gets PLUS_EXTRA) and Pro (sonnet). Guidance is never sent to non-UK users (ES/US/IE/FR, including a mocked chat with country=ES). Nation filtering is correct (Wales s.173 rule only for wales, LRA rule only for northern_ireland, GB ET rule not sent for NI). Glasgow resident renting in Cardiff gets the Wales rule in a mocked chat. Fact-pack sign-off is not bypassed: lex_guidance does not import lex_lessons or touch the DB, and 0/38 packs are signed off. Citation guard: landmark kept, volume citation kept, invented cases removed with no fragments, wrong citation on a real case stripped, customer-quoted fake labelled, separate mentions do not count as support, SOURCES line pruned, 'England v Wales' untouched. Legislation: Welsh bilingual titles resolve, SIs are labelled 'existence checked only', ACT_TTL is 3 days. A live check confirmed SI 2026/954 commences ERA 2025 s.152 and Sch.12 from 1 Oct 2026 for relevant dates on or after that day, so the guidance text is accurate. Deadlines: 1 Oct boundary correct (30 Sep -> 3 months, 1 Oct -> 31 Mar 2027 citing SI 2026/954); claim types, NI/LRA wording, ALREADY PASSED/URGENT/APPROXIMATE/INDEPENDENT CHECK and parking unknown-service all behave as described. Eval scenarios: 40 scenarios, date 2026-11-18, all labelled, 8 CORRECTIONS.

critical.issue: KeyError when the customer writes 'Last Week' or 'LAST MONTH' (or any capitalised 'week'/'month'). Line 515 looks up the dict with m.group(3), which is not lowercased, while the regex is re.I. build_deadlines raises, and the server's try/except at ~2224/~2439 then drops BOTH the deadline block AND lex_guidance.block() (official rules + sourced case list) from the system prompt. Reproduced in a mocked chat: log shows 'Deadline block failed: 'Week''. With lowercase 'last week' the same chat works. In production this path is reached once the Haiku extraction returns calcs.

minor.issue: When jurisdiction is unknown, the function returns before adding the 'CLAIM TYPE NOT CONFIRMED' warning, the SI 2026/954 / 3-month explanation and the series/continuing-act caveat. The safe date itself is correct: min(GB, NI) = 19 Jan 2027 for an act on 20 Oct 2026.

'Immigration Rules 2024 and the Civil Procedure Rules 1998' becomes ONE SI title, because years count as SI words and 'and/the' connectors are allowed. The Immigration/Civil skip then fails and the merged title gets a not_found flag, a [⚠ see legislation check] marker and a CONFIDENCE downgrade. 'Child Arrangements Order 2025' (a court order) is also existence-checked as an SI and would be flagged.
'S.S.I. 2026/12' (a Scottish SI) is matched as 'S.I. 2026/12' and looked up under /uksi/. That would wrongly mark it not found.

Uses a substring test in both directions, so a wrong citation that is a prefix of the real one is accepted. Example: 'ParkingEye Ltd v Beavis [2015] UKSC 6' is kept (real: UKSC 67); likewise '[1997] UKHL 4' for Bolitho (real: UKHL 46). The solo-citation check 'lcite in src' has the same prefix weakness.

Ordinary 'X v Y' sentences are treated as cases. 'I watched Arsenal v Chelsea with my landlord' becomes 'I watched a court decision (reference removed …)'. Only nation names and a few words are in _CASE_STOP.

Prefix-only word boundary: 'Parkinson's disease' matches 'park' and puts ParkingEye/Beavis into the prompt (prompt noise only). Similarly 'court' matches 'courtesy', 'sue' matches 'suede', and 'tribunal' pulls employment cases into immigration-tribunal questions.

action_items: HIGH: deadline_calc.relative_dates line 515: use m.group(3).lower(). Also consider moving lex_guidance.block() (and _fact_pack_block) out of the try that wraps build_deadlines in server.py ~2224/~2439, so a deadline failure cannot silently remove the official-source rules.
deadline_calc._et: in the unknown-nation branch, append the CLAIM TYPE NOT CONFIRMED / date-of-act / continuing-act notes, as in the confirmed-nation path.

legal_sources._SI_RE: do not let a 4-digit year be a title word directly after 'Rules|Regulations|Order', or split at the first ' (Rules|Regulations|Order) YYYY'. Skip court orders such as 'Child Arrangements Order', 'Non-Molestation Order', 'Possession Order'.
legal_sources._SI_NUM: exclude 'S.S.I.', 'W.S.I.' and 'SSI' (or route them to /ssi/ and /wsi/).
landmark_cases.cite_matches: compare whole citations (for example normalised equality, or a match on the citation number with a word boundary) instead of a two-way substring test.
Optional: add sports or ordinary-usage words to _CASE_STOP, and use \b on both ends of the lex_guidance topic regexes (e.g. park(?:ing)?\b).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py ~2224/~2439: one try block covers deadline building, the fact pack and lex_guidance. Any exception in deadline code silently removes the official-source rules (confirmed by the 'Last Week' KeyError).
deadline_calc._parking uses datetime.now() instead of the 'today' passed to compute_annotated. This is inconsistent and makes the code harder to test.
lex_guidance.block limits rules to rules[:5] and case_lines takes the first 6 cases in list order, not by relevance. A multi-topic question can lose the most relevant rule or case.

tests/test_lex_routing.py hardcodes MONGO_URL and DB_NAME and does a live signup plus real LLM calls through the public URL. This is an environment limitation under AIA_NO_PAID=1, not a defect; NOT run.

test_stage2_safety Glasgow/Cardiff: the old expectation (conflict=True, applicable=None) came from before Phase 2D. Phase 2D made housing follow the property's nation, so conflict=False and applicable='wales' is correct. The old expectation was outdated; this is not a defect.

success_rate.backend: Existing suites 100% (418/418) + offline eval 117/117; new probes 23/34 (11 fail: 1 medium defect, the rest minor regex false positives)

seed_data_creation: None persistent. The mk fixture creates temporary TEST users for the mocked chat tests and deletes them by id.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run each test file in a separate pytest invocation with AIA_NO_PAID=1. The probe file tests/test_phase2e_probe_iter54.py marks each known defect with 'PROBE'. After the main agent fixes them, all 34 should pass. Do not run tests/test_lex_routing.py (paid LLM calls). The server date is 18 Nov 2026.
rca of the issue: Repro: chat message 'I was dismissed Last Week by my employer in Leeds. What is my tribunal deadline?' with the extraction returning one ET calc. _REL matches 'Last Week' with re.I, so group(3) is 'Week'. The dict {'week':…, 'month':…}['Week'] raises KeyError. build_deadlines does not catch exceptions from relative_dates, so the error reaches the server try/except, which logs 'Deadline block failed' and skips the system_msg addition that also carries lex_guidance.block. Fix: lower() group(3), and separate the guidance wiring from the deadline try.
